CITY COUNCIL
MINUTES
CITY OF BALDWIN PARK
CITY COUNCIL
WEDNESDAY, MAY 05, 2010
7:00 p.m. COUNCIL CHAMBERS
14403 E. Pacific Avenue
Baldwin Park
Manuel Lozano, Mayor/Chair
Ricardo Pacheco, Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Marlen Garcia, Monica Garcia, Susan Rubio Council Members/Members
Maria Contreras, City Treasurer Alejandra Avila, City Clerk
The CITY COUNCIL of the City of Baldwin Park met in REGULAR SESSION at the above time and place.
CALL TO ORDER
INVOCATION
Led by Pastor Jackson
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
ANNOUNCEMENTS
Mayor Lozano closed in memory of Paul Garcia and Ms. McGee, two senior participants from the Community Center
Council member Monica Garcia expressed her sadness in the passing of Mr. Garcia and Ms. McGee. She also closed in memory of Roberta Lightfoot, former Baldwin Park resident. Councilmember Rubio spoke favorably of Ms. Lightfoot and expressed her condolences
ROLL CALL
Present: Councilmember Marlen Garcia, Councilmember Monica Garcia, Councilmember Rubio, Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco, Mayor Lozano.
Absent: None.
Also Present: Chief Executive Officer Singhal, City Attorney Pannone, Recreation & Community Services Director Carrillo, Community Development Manager Castagnola, Public Works Director Galvez, Chief Hadsell, Finance Director Quijano, City Clerk Avila, City Treasurer Contreras, Deputy City Clerk Nieto.
PROCLAMATIONS, COMMENDATIONS & PRESENTATIONS
Recognition of Baldwin Park High School Basketball Coach Marc Hart and the Baldwin Park High School Girls Basketball team
Presentation was deferred to the next meeting, with correction that it was the boys basketball team that would be recognized
Presentation and comments by Duarte Mayor Margaret E. Finlay on mosquito and vector control districts
Presentation was deferred
Presentation by the Mark Daniel Flores Music Foundation to music scholarship recipients Maria Arias, Andres Meza and Kevin Phan of Sierra Vista High School and Melissa Ramirez of Baldwin Park High School
Mr. and Mrs. Flores shared background on the foundation and scholarship, introduced the scholarship recipients and thanked the City Council for all of their support
Presentation of Proclamation proclaiming May 9th - 15th as Poppy Week in the City of Baldwin Park to Clarissa Salcido, 2010 Miss Poppy
Mayor Lozano read the proclamation and presented it to Miss Poppy
Proclamation proclaiming May as Older Americans Month in the City of Baldwin Park
Mayor Lozano read the proclamation and presented it to the senior citizens who were in attendance at the meeting
Recognition of Baldwin Park Police Chief Lili Hadsell for being named "Woman of Distinction" by Congresswoman Judy Chu; Amber Guadez, Baldwin Park High School for being named "Emerging Young Leader" by Assemblyman Ed Hernandez, and Lizete Avila, Baldwin Park High School for being named "Youth Trailblazer" by Senator Gloria Romero
Mayor Lozano, joined by the Council, Clerk and Treasurer presented certificates and flowers to the honorees. Each honoree shared some words with the audience . Mayor Lozano announced that their names would be placed on the marquee at Morgan Park
Mayor Lozano thanked the SCE Credit Union for the presentation that they had given on money management skills for youth. He asked the Credit Union to host a function for Baldwin Park residents and asked that the information be placed in the NOW
Councilmember Monica Garcia gave accolades to Ms. Guadez and Ms. Avila on their respective recognitions, noting their academic and leadership accomplishments. Councilmember Rubio also mentioned that Ms. Guadez served as a student representative on the Baldwin Park Unified School District Board of Education
Mayor Lozano welcomed back Baldwin Park Police Lt. Joe Cowan
Councilmember Marlen Garcia requested that the Baldwin Park High School girls and boys wrestling teams be recognized at a future Council meeting, noting that one of the girls had qualified for the Junior Olympic Team. She spoke about Coach Mike Duran’s commitment to the youth participants
Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco wished the audience a happy cinco de mayo. He spoke about census participation and encouraged residents to continue striving for a higher rate of return on the 2010 Census
PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS
Elisa Clifford , SCE Region Manager presented the state of the utility and provided information to the Council
Rafael Garcia, Baldwin Park Library, congratulated the evening's honorees and thanked the Mayor, Council, Director Carrillo and staff for their various contributions to the library
Mark Vega , resident spoke about the building code transition and asked for the Mayor’s help to facilitate the sale of his property
Greg Tuttle , business owner thanked Mayor Lozano for allowing him to speak at the recent budget meeting and addressed comments made by Councilmember Marlen Garcia regarding the Redflex cameras
Cruz Baca , resident congratulated the young ladies on their recognitions and hoped their successes continued; she congratulated those involved in the recent immigration rallies. On behalf of Charlie Contreras, she noted that his name should also be included on the petition provided in the staff report on sound walls
Public Communications were closed at 7:47 p.m.

Moved by Councilmember Marlen Garcia, seconded by Mayor Lozano.

Request by Councilmember Monica Garcia for discussion on the following:
Council discussion and direction to staff to coordinate a tree-planting event in conjunction with an AQMD grant
Councilmember Monica Garcia spoke about the grant opportunity for drought tolerant trees to be planted in the City, which was aligned with the Council’s green vision for the City. She thanked CEO Singhal and Associate Planner Lopez for processing the grant application in July 2009 and again in October 2009 and reported that at least a couple of hundred trees would be purchased to be planted along Francisquito Avenue. She spoke about a proposed Earth Day event that had to be pushed back for scheduling reasons and asked that staff work on a future tree-planting event. This would engage the community and include, at the suggestion of City Treasurer Contreras, the dedication of at least three trees to fallen Baldwin Park servicemen and/or women.
She asked that this be an extended event in conjunction with Memorial Day and that it not be scaled back
Council discussion and direction to staff to pursue grant funding through the Safe Routes to School Program, a reimbursement funding program for reducing injuries and fatalities through capital projects that improve safety for children in grades K – 12 who walk or bicycle to school
Councilmember Monica Garcia directed staff to pursue the Safe Routes to School grant opportunity due in July. She spoke about the grant opportunities and their many benefits. Through CEO Singhal she requested that staff look into applying for these grant funds to promote a healthy and safe community, especially around the schools
Request by Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco for discussion on the following:
Council discussion and consideration to adopt a resolution enacting an economic boycott of the State of Arizona for the recent adoption of SB1070 pertaining to immigration law
Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco spoke about recent legislation that had been enacted in the State of Arizona (SB 1070.) He said that even though Baldwin Park was a small city, it would be a symbolic gesture to show its opposition to this type of legislation through an economic boycott of the state.
He expressed the understanding that immigration was an emotional issue and believed that there were better options to give everyone a fair chance to come to this country through the proper channels. He requested that Council direct staff to bring forward a resolution enacting an economic boycott of the State of Arizona.
Mayor Lozano spoke about the rallys that had been organized in opposition to SB 1070 and the message being sent by Arizona Governor Jan Brewer by enacting this legislation, that, in his opinion was divisive.
He expressed that during the times of recession, this legislation could potentially lead to blame being placed on a particular race or group of people. He shared a conversation that he had with a Baldwin Park resident who served the United States in the military and said that he was mad at what had taken place.
Mayor Lozano stated that there is no other country on earth like American and that Southern California was a melting pot, further making the country unique. He expressed the opinion that the courts would overturn this law and that in the end, all Americans would win. He stated his desire to host a peaceful rally, with all Councilmembers present, so that the East Valley could voice its opposition to SB 1070
Councilmember Marlen Garcia stated that she was in support of any steps that the Council might take to oppose a racist law. She referred to an email message that she had received from an Assemblymember in Arizona, requesting a letter of opposition to SB 1070.
She shared a childhood experience in which her parents were not sold milk in the state of Texas because they were Mexican. She said that she reminded her children every day that racism still exists and was thriving in this country, noting that even with the election of President Obama, people were still not coming together for the betterment of the country.
She expressed that the community needed to unite in opposition to SB 1070 and requested that a letter of opposition be drafted.
Councilmember Rubio expressed her strong agreement with all of the comments made by her Council colleagues. She stated that SB 1070 legislation was a basic violation of human rights and unacceptable discrimination, and it would possibly become a safety issue for everyone.
She stated her fear that this type of legislation would dissuade individuals from coming forward with information on crimes, for fear of being arrested, and that basic crimes would be even more difficult to solve. She said that every single person would be impacted by this type of law.
Chief Hadsell assured everyone that the Police Department never inquired on the legal status of individuals who seek assistance and report crimes. The Baldwin Park Police Department’s only concern was to keep the community safe.
Councilmember Rubio reiterated her fear that people may not come forward to report crimes or provide information that would lead to the solving of basic crimes and that the message of this legislation may be misunderstood.
Mayor Lozano expressed the opinion that nothing would be done on the Federal level because of mid-term elections and read an excerpt from the Los Angeles Times related to arrests made in Maricopa County in Arizona.
Councilmember Monica Garcia joined her Council colleagues in solidarity, through whatever efforts are taken, to send a message to Arizona that the Council opposed SB 1070. She stated that she would not be supporting Arizona in any way and encouraged those who felt strongly and opposed the law to boycott the state of Arizona if they can avoid it.
She expressed her concern that, as a Mexican-American she may be vulnerable to profiling, noting that .
